svg.aria-label: mensurflow auto-tuning: Tuner::tune records the algorithm's calls, and for each distinct call searches the kernel's space of settings with binary sampling, timing each point (checked against the default's result, median of samples, early stop), confirms the fastest few against the default, chooses devices for Execution::Auto ops, checks the whole algorithm and saves a text file; Algorithm::run with the tuner applies the stored settings and devices in dispatch.
svg.text: Auto-tuning: minimizing time(arguments ; kernel parameters)
For each call, the parameters (m, n, k, threads) are fixed and the arguments (the kernel's settings) take a few ordered values each. Offline, on this machine; results go to a text file.
1 · TUNING, ONCE
tuner.tune(algorithm, inputs, options)
src/core/tuning.cpp
Record the calls
algorithm.run(inputs) once, inside a TuningScope{record}: dispatch() records every op call:
the op, the execution asked for, where the data is, where it ran, its arguments (RecordedCall).
Each distinct call
key: machine · op · device · kernel version · m n k (+ threads on the CPU)
Already in the file (and not retune) → reused, nothing is measured. Otherwise steps 3 to 6.
The space of the call
space(args): one region per kernel variant, each with ordered axes (the arguments);
allowed(args, config): drops points the kernel cannot run or that make no sense for the call.
Metal matmul: simdgroup (bm bn bk sg_m sg_n) · tiled (bm bn bk tm tn) · MPS: 1,114 points at 1024³
CPU matmul: rows · depth · cols, values cut to the matrix: 80 points at 512³
Reference
a GPU is kept busy for 1 s first: its clock rises only under load
The defaults run once; their outputs are the result every other point must match.
Search
detail::search(space, method, measure)
The method asks for points in batches (the samples of one line, or a region's grid);
each new point goes to the objective (A), and the search keeps the lowest time.
binary sampling, the default (B) · exhaustive: every allowed point
Confirm
the default and the 3 fastest points, timed again together
3 rounds, the order rotated each round; the median of the rounds picks the winner and
gives default_ms → best_ms. Points were timed seconds apart, and a GPU's clock moves
(a 1024³ Metal default: 0.85 to 1.21 ms between runs). The winner is stored for the call.
Device choice
for every op called with Execution::Auto
Each device with a kernel is timed through dispatch(), copies there and back included,
after its own settings were tuned; it must agree with the CPU's result. Fastest → gpu=0 or gpu=1.
512³ matmul with the data on the CPU: gpu 0.77 ms vs cpu 1.68 ms; a 65,536-element add stays on the CPU.
Check the whole algorithm, save
Timed without and with the results (at least 0.2 s each, median). Slower with them →
everything this tune added is dropped. Then the file is written.
A The objective: the time at one point
measure() → median_ms()
Measured already?
yes → the remembered time (the search may ask for a point twice)
Run once: same result as the default?
no → rejected: ∞, never timed (within 1e-3 · max|value|)
Time it: the median of samples
1 warm-up run
caches; on Metal, the pipeline compiled for these tiles
1 run to estimate
repeats per sample so that one sample lasts at least 1 ms
samples
until at least 3 samples and 50 ms (at most 1,000); each run waits for the GPU
after 3 samples, fastest > 1.3 × the best median so far → stop: it cannot win
result
the median sample, so one slow sample does not move it
512³ CPU matmul (≈1.4 ms): ≈35 samples, ≈38 runs a point. Early stop: 1024³ Metal search 2.0–2.7 s → 0.9–1.1 s.
B Binary sampling, on two of the CPU matmul's arguments
S

g.text: 512³, rows held; start S = the default
Pass 1, depth: sample the row through S
coarse to fine; S is the middle (level 1)
all measured → move to the fastest: depth 32
Pass 1, cols: the column through it
pass 2: lines through the new point;
21 of 80 points measured, 2 s; 5 of 5 runs
Every sample is measured; no comparison of two
noisy times throws half a line away (a binary
search did, on a plateau, and ended at 1.65 ms).

svg.text: C The results file
plain text, one line per call under its machine; readable and editable
# mensurflow tuning results
machine Apple M3 Pro | Apple M3 Pro
matmul cpu v1 m=512 n=512 k=512 threads=11 -> rows=0 depth=32 cols=512 | 1.44 ms (default 2.02 ms) tested
matmul auto v1 data=cpu f32 512x512 512x512 -> gpu=1 | 0.77 ms (default 1.68 ms) tested
one form for both: a device choice is device "auto", setting gpu; keyed exactly (size ranges: not done yet)
2 · USING THE RESULTS, EVERY RUN
algorithm.run(inputs, tuner)
dispatch() in src/core/dispatcher.cpp
TuningScope{cache}
opened by run(); thread_local, so
only this run's ops see the results
the algorithm's code is unchanged
Execution::Auto ops
a stored "auto" line for the op, data
device, dtype, shapes → gpu=0 or gpu=1
none stored → the CPU, as without a tuner
Tunable kernel
apply_tuning(): find(machine, op, device,
version, key) in the file
none → the kernel's defaults
OpArgs::tuning
the settings as values in the
kernel's parameter order
(TuningConfig, up to 8)
The kernel reads them
CPU: rows, depth, cols tile sizes
Metal: variant and tiles; its pipeline
is compiled once and cached
read when the Tuner is made
